title: Two Decades of Research Progress in Resource Allocation for PLC Systems: From Core Concepts to Frontiers
affiliation: Federal University of Juiz de Fora, Federal University of Paraná, Federal University of Rio de Janeiro, Alpen-Adria University Klagenfurt
domain: Power Line Communication / Resource Allocation / OFDM / Smart Grid
paper_type: Comprehensive Historical Survey with Dual-Perspective Taxonomy

analysis_policy.focus: Extract dual-perspective taxonomy pattern, chronological review methodology, and lessons learned synthesis
analysis_policy.depth: Full paper analysis including 9 sections, dual taxonomies, and 20-year chronological review

section_flow.title: Introduction
subsections: Motivation and Comparison With Other Surveys
section_flow.summary: Motivates RA for PLC systems as enabling technology for smart grid, home networking, and in-vehicle communications. Positions paper using two comparison tables (Table I: RA surveys, Table II: PLC surveys) showing gap in RA+PLC combined coverage.
key_claims: PLC systems have achieved significant maturity over a century
Electric power systems impose severe constraints on data communication
First comprehensive survey combining PLC and RA fundamentals with dual-methodology approach
Covers single- and multi-user scenarios with chronological progression

section_flow.title: Power Line Communication
section_flow.summary: Provides PLC fundamentals: motivations (ubiquity, channel capacity, vehicle applications, sensing), characteristics (EMI, attenuation, load dynamics), limitations (connection points, cable count), and regulatory constraints.
key_claims: Frequency band up to 100 MHz offers channel capacity over 1 Gbps
Channel capacities beyond 1 Tbps possible with power lines as waveguides up to 100 GHz
PLC systems are secondary spectrum users with PSD mask constraints

section_flow.title: A PLC-Centric Taxonomy of Resource Allocation
section_flow.summary: First taxonomy perspective: organizes RA works by PLC-specific criteria (voltage level, frequency band, channel/noise model, environment, application). Includes percentage distribution figures for each dimension.
key_claims: LV electric power systems most investigated due to indoor/outdoor coverage
BB-PLC research dominates due to data rate demands
LTI channel model most adopted despite LPTV reality
Home networking is primary application, followed by Smart Grid

section_flow.title: Optimization-Oriented View of Resource Allocation
section_flow.summary: Second taxonomy perspective: frames RA as optimization problem with four components (objective functions, constraints, resources, CSI). Details rate-adaptive vs margin-adaptive criteria.
key_claims: Four components: objective functions, constraints, resources, CSI
Rate-adaptive most adopted criterion
Resources: frequency, time, power/bits, code
nSNR coherence bandwidth is crucial parameter for multicarrier PLC

section_flow.title: Resource Allocation in Single-User Systems
section_flow.summary: Chronological review of single-user RA (2003-2022). Covers bit-loading algorithms (water-filling, Chow's, Levin-Campello), LPTV channel exploitation, and complexity reduction techniques.
key_claims: Peak research activity 2006-2018
TCRA, SCRA, STCRA techniques for complexity reduction
nSNR coherence bandwidth introduced in 2017
Hybrid PLC/WLC systems emerged post-2020

section_flow.title: Resource Allocation in Multi-User Systems
section_flow.summary: Chronological review of multi-user RA (2000-2020). Covers OFDMA evolution, cross-layer approaches, cooperative communication, NOMA integration, and hybrid PLC-VLC systems.
key_claims: Research concentrated 2006-2019, aligned with IEEE/ITU-T standardization
Three types of data rate maximization: sum rate, weighted sum, min-user
Post-2015 shift toward Smart Grid applications
NOMA adoption emerged in 2019

section_flow.title: Remarks and Lessons Learned
section_flow.summary: Synthesizes key findings: RA evolution from static to dynamic schemes, channel model challenges, application-specific requirements, hybrid system opportunities.
key_claims: RA evolved from simple/static to sophisticated/dynamic schemes
Non-uniformity in channel modeling is serious concern
Hybrid PLC+WLC systems are strong research direction
Energy efficiency and privacy constraints not yet adequately addressed

section_flow.title: Research Opportunities
section_flow.summary: Identifies research gaps: AI/ML integration, 6G compatibility, Age of Information metrics, impedance matching, in-band full duplex, semantic communications.
key_claims: AI/ML for solving complex non-convex RA problems
AoI metric for freshness-constrained applications
Impedance matching constraint in RA formulation
Semantic communications as future direction

section_flow.title: Conclusions
section_flow.summary: Concludes with emphasis on dual-perspective taxonomy approach and chronological narrative contribution.

rhetorical_contract.promise: Provide comprehensive 20-year historical survey on RA for PLC systems using dual-perspective taxonomy and chronological narrative
rhetorical_contract.delivery_mechanism: PLC-centric taxonomy → Optimization-centric taxonomy → Single-user chronology → Multi-user chronology → Lessons learned → Future directions
rhetorical_contract.unique_contribution: First survey combining PLC fundamentals with RA fundamentals using complementary perspectives and chronological evolution tracking

synthesis.integration_approach: Dual-perspective complementary taxonomy followed by chronological narrative

gap_identification: AI/ML for complex non-convex RA problems
lessons_learned: RA evolved from static to dynamic schemes

Hybrid PLC+WLC systems offer best of both worlds

reusable_writing_recipes.description: Present two complementary taxonomies from different viewpoints to provide comprehensive coverage: one domain-centric (PLC-centric) and one methodology-centric (optimization-centric)
structure: Each perspective organized with multiple dimensions
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Section III (PLC-centric: voltage, frequency, noise, environment, application) + Section IV (Optimization: objectives, constraints, resources, CSI)
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Provides multiple entry points for readers; shows technical depth from different angles; accommodates different reader backgrounds
reusable_writing_recipes.complexity: High - requires deep expertise in both domain and methodology

reusable_writing_recipes.recipe_name: Year-by-Year Chronological Narrative with Era Groupings
reusable_writing_recipes.description: Organize literature review as year-by-year progression grouped into thematic eras, with each era introduced by a contextual paragraph
structure: Era introduction paragraph (e.g., '2003-2009', '2010-2015', '2016+') with thematic summary
Year-by-year bullet points within each era
Each year entry summarizes key papers with context and limitations
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Sections V and VI organize 20 years of research into 3 eras each, with detailed year-by-year entries

reusable_writing_recipes.description: For each chronological section, include a summary table with optimization-specific metadata: convexity, solution/algorithm, optimality

reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Enables quick algorithmic comparisons; highlights optimization approach evolution; facilitates reproducibility assessment
reusable_writing_recipes.complexity: Medium - requires technical analysis of each paper

reusable_writing_recipes.recipe_name: Percentage Distribution Figures Per Taxonomy Dimension

reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Quantifies research effort distribution; identifies under-explored areas; provides evidence for gap claims

reusable_writing_recipes.description: End each major section with an explicit 'Takeaways' subsection synthesizing key insights
structure: Highlights main findings from the section
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Subsections II-E, III-F, IV-E, V-C, VI-C all end with Takeaways

reusable_writing_recipes.recipe_name: Dual Survey Comparison Tables in Introduction
reusable_writing_recipes.description: Present two comparison tables in introduction: one for related surveys on the methodology (RA) and one for related surveys on the domain (PLC)
structure: Table I: RA surveys across different technologies (DSL, WLC, VLC, PLC)
Table II: PLC surveys with RA coverage indicator
'This survey' row in both tables showing comprehensive coverage
Narrative explaining the gap at intersection
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Tables I and II in Section I-A showing limited RA+PLC intersection
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Clearly establishes novelty; shows awareness of both fields; justifies dual-perspective approach

key_concepts.resource_allocation: Optimization of limited resources (frequency, time, power, code) within communication systems to meet QoS requirements
key_concepts.nSNR_coherence_bandwidth: Maximum frequency bandwidth in which same amount of power and bits can be allocated; key parameter for multicarrier PLC over AC systems
key_concepts.lptv_channel: Linear Periodically Time Variant channel model capturing cyclostationary behavior synchronous to mains frequency
